args: Sensitivity check (J after the D3c interview), its rule written before it runs: out/_analysis/d4a01_kind_collapsed.py computes distance.py's distance once more on the same shared lines and prior.md's weights and grades, with every add-condition, add-step and restrict line given one kind, 'collapsed', in place of its adjudicated kind (so two different ops among the three grade 0.5, and any of them against another kind's op 0). It compares the result with _views/distance.tsv: Pearson and Spearman over room pairs, the mean absolute difference, the delta score under seed 0, and the ARI between the two average-linkage trees at 2, 3, 5, 8 and 12 clusters. Nothing in _views/ is touched. No cut rests on the adjudicated kind of those three ops; their keys are read in the all-kinds matrices.

Sensitivity check read (out/_analysis/d4a01_kind_collapsed/, .txt). With kind collapsed for add-condition, add-step and restrict (5,638 of the 26,487 shared lines: add-condition 178 elaboration and 1,045 specification; add-step 428, 991 and 2 corrections; restrict 26, 2,952 and 16 corrections), the combined distance moves little: Pearson 0.9965 and Spearman 0.9967 over 248,160 room pairs, 153,437 pairs changed, mean absolute difference 0.0024; the delta score 0.4223 against the carried 0.4227. The average-linkage trees agree at 2 and 3 clusters (ARI 1.00), and less at finer cuts: 0.886 at 5, 0.922 at 8, 0.779 at 12. Reading: the combined distance and its coarse groups do not rest on the adjudicated kind of those ops; the per-kind views do, since for add-step and add-condition the specification lines outnumber the elaboration lines about 2 to 1 and 6 to 1. So no cut reads a branch's membership from the per-kind matrices for those ops; keys are read in the all-kinds matrices, and a branch's kind field is reported as the kind of its members' lines, not relied on.

Cut rules, written before the first cut (stage D4 section 2); they go into tree-D4.md before any branch. (R0) Minimum group size: the default, 5; prior.md sets none, and I keep it, since 720 level-3 keys are held by 5 to 19 rooms and a higher floor would drop most change keys before reading them. (R1) A branch is keyed on an element's change key (op add-step, add-condition, link, restrict or contradict), read in the all-kinds matrix (the kind of add-condition, add-step and restrict lines is not relied on), at the deepest ladder level where 5 or more rooms meet on it. Arrow keys cannot key a branch (stage_D4.py resolves a key's target against the elements) and are read as context. Instantiate and absent keys specify; they change nothing, so they define no branch. (R2) A key becomes a branch only if the members' lines, read through out/_analysis/d4_key_lines.py, state one shared change to the element (a step, a condition or a link the statement does not hold, or holds only in part); otherwise the group is set aside with its reason. (R3) A subform is a level-3 child key held by 5 or more of the branch's members whose lines state a narrower change than the parent's. (R4) Corrections that meet only at the dimension or the bare target (P05's shape read, R01's joining) are groupings, not branches. (R5) A room in two branches that do not nest is a cross-link, generated by script with both keys as its reason. (R6) Order: by element, from the largest change-key group at level 4 downward; a leg ends at a safe stop after a logged move. (R7) The ground is the keys unless a cut's tier_history line declares the members' material. The branch's kind field is the majority kind of its members' lines on the key, reported and not relied on.

Cut rules, amendment R1a (D4a-02, 25 October; forward only, and F01 already meets it, since its largest child holds 37 of 103 rooms): where a level-4 change key's rooms are mostly one level-3 child (that child holds 80 per cent or more of them), the branch is declared at the third order on the child key, the deepest level where its members meet; otherwise at the fourth order, with children of 5 rooms or more as candidate subforms under R3. R1b: several change keys of one element whose rooms overlap are read together; where the same rooms carry two keys and their lines state one change, the branch takes both keys (a multi-key definition), otherwise each key is read on its own. R1c: a group whose lines restate a condition or step the element's statement already holds changes nothing and is set aside under R2, whatever kind the lines were ruled.

Decide from the record; if a join is defensible, make it as D4 cuts and say how D5 is organized (one leg per parent); if not, say why in notes-D4.md and change nothing (D5 one leg per branch). J will not be asked again. Read AGENT.md, the head, STAGE-D4 (unchanged), diary --last 5, validate --open D4 (the same literal-pattern error). The test, written before any computation: a parent must be a branch the stage allows. (1) It is grounded on keys its members all hold at its level (section 2; the material never stands alone). (2) A subform nests by adding keys, and stage_D4.py accepts a child only if each parent key has the same op and target as a child key and the child's node lifts to the parent's node; so a parent can join only branches of one element and one op. (3) A group that meets only at the dimension or the bare target is a grouping, not a branch (section 2; cut rule R4). (4) No list of rooms that belong together may come from anywhere but the ledger, so co-membership alone grounds no parent. The handler's two facts are checked by script, not adopted.

The join check (out/_analysis/d4a04_joins.py, its output d4a04_joins.txt). The handler's facts, checked: 25 top-level branches on 14 elements; by the elements' own dimension field D02 9, D07 5, D03 4, D04 4, D06 2, D01 1, as the handler says, but by the dimension each branch's key lifts to D02 9, D04 6, D07 6, D06 2, D01 1, D03 1 (F07 lifts to D02, F26 to D04, F32 to D07), and the ladder joins by the key's lift, not the element's field. Joins the stage allows: a parent needs keys every member holds, and stage_D4.py nests a child only under a key of the same op and target. Only three sets share element and op. P04 add-step (F15, F33) meet first at the dimension, add-step:P04:D02, 85 rooms, 20 in neither child. P16 add-condition (F22, F28) meet at the dimension, add-condition:P16:D04, 65 rooms, 13 in neither child. P05 restrict (F07, F26, F27) meet only at the bare target, restrict:P05:*, 214 rooms, 106 in none of them. Each is a grouping under section 2 and cut rule R4, and each would bring in rooms whose lines were never read for the shared change (R2). The families that span ops or elements (P05's clause and the marking; the shared instruction; carrying on; the chat; machine hands; the frame; help) have no common key, and rooms in all of their branches number 0 to 5, so no parent can be grounded on keys, and co-membership alone may not ground one. Decision: no join is defensible; nothing changes; D5 runs as the stage says, one leg per branch.
